unlisted_practices: Develop collaborative, uniform pediatric data repositories holding practice data from diverse geographic and demographic contexts.
Build AI system integration on existing health information infrastructure and use open-source platforms for compatibility.
Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and audit trails to protect pediatric health data.
Use privacy-enhancing technologies such as federated learning and anonymization for collaborative AI model development.
Provide informed consent processes that respect individual and community autonomy, including the right to opt out of data use for AI development.
Invest strategically in digital infrastructure, including connectivity, computing resources, and technical capacity, in underserved regions.
Use co-design approaches engaging local communities and health workers to ensure cultural appropriateness and language accessibility.
Prioritize AI applications addressing high-burden pediatric conditions.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint paper discussing frameworks, opportunities, and governance/implementation challenges for integrating AI in pediatric care.
